newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ACCC sees Bank of Melbourne branch closes.
newsitem.headline: ACCC sees Bank of Melbourne branch closes.

text.p: The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said on Friday it expected the Westpac Banking Corp merger with Bank of Melbourne Ltd (BML) would lead to BML branch closures in Victoria.
"It is clear there will be some overlap and as a result it is likely there will be some (branch) closures," ACCC chairman Alan Fels told a media briefing.
Fels said the branch closures, from a consumer point of view, would reduce costs and increase competition in the Victorian market.
"The ACCC did not seek any undertakings (from Westpac about branch closures) here, we didn't think it would be appropriate," Fels added.

As earlier reported, the two banks did give the ACCC a range of undertakings in seeking approval of their merger, including that the autonomy of BML management would be retained and that normal opening hours and local debit card operations would be kept.
Westpac and BML earlier said they had received approval from the Reserve Bank of Australia and the ACCC for the merger.
